title: Version Control
description: Track every meaningful change to your project with git — commit snapshots with messages that explain why, undo the three kinds of mistakes you'll actually make, work on something risky without breaking what already works, and keep a copy of your project somewhere that isn't only your laptop.

title: Checking Your Own Work
description: Write tests that tell you when you break something — starting from why re-clicking through your app by hand stops working as it grows, through your first automated test, testing the edges instead of just the easy middle, making sure a test can actually fail, and running the whole suite without having to remember to.

title: Organising a Project
description: Structure a project so you can find things and change one part safely — knowing when one file has actually become too many jobs at once, splitting code into modules for a real reason, naming files and folders for someone arriving cold, separating configuration from code, and writing a README that lets a stranger actually run what you built.

title: Reading Other People's Code
description: Understand code you didn't write well enough to actually change it — where to start in an unfamiliar project, following one specific thing through it end to end, using search and jump-to-definition instead of scrolling blind, making a small change safely, and being honest with yourself about the difference between recognizing code and actually understanding it.

title: Debugging Properly
description: Find the actual cause of a bug by narrowing it down deliberately, not by guessing — reproducing it reliably first, halving the search space instead of scanning randomly, choosing between printing values and a real debugger, catching the assumption that's wrong instead of just the code, and writing a test that captures the bug so it can never silently come back.
